To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the unitarity of the scattering matrix is a consequence of the unitarity of a covariant, non-local effective field theory.

the effective field theory approach is the correct way to describe the intermediate energy regime of strong interactions and that the effective field-operators for fermionic and boson resonances are consistent with the unitarity of the S-matrix.

the unitary effective field theory of intermediate energy strong interaction can be consistently described by a field-theoretic picture of effective degrees of freedom, i.e. resonances, which are described by effective field-operators obeying Wick's Theorem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a relativistic effective field theory of intermediate energy physics, which is based on an unitary description of resonances as effective degrees of freedom.

the development of a consistent effective field-theory description of nucleonic and other resonances in a unitary relativistic quantum field theory framework, and the application of this framework to phenomenology.
the development of an unitary relativist field theoretic approach for the effective description of nucleon and resonance degrees of freedom in intermediate energy strong interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effective degrees of freedom of intermediate energy QCD are ``effective'' field-operators which obey unitarity and Wick's theorem.
the EFT approach is a very powerful tool to describe strong interaction physics at intermediate energies.
a relativistic unitary EFT of resonances is the most consistent way to describe strong interaction physics at intermediate energies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ``toy-model'' of a unitary EFT of resonances can be considered as a ``proof of principle'' for a consistent description of nucleonic resonance physics in an unitary field-theoretic framework.
the unitarity and the renormalization properties of a relativistic EFT of strong interaction at the intermediate energy scale are consistently described within a covariant framework.
the effective field-theoretic description of nucleonic resonance physics is consistent with the picture of an EFT of strong interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a consistent description of resonances in an EFT is possible and that the EFT is not just an ``effective'' but a ``complete'' theory.
the description of resonances in terms of effective field-operators is consistent with unitarity, locality and renormalizability.
a relativistic unitary EFT for resonances can be constructed in a consistent and systematic way.
